monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady fever in a room I cannot see. Three cycles of pressing have left The Fat Anchor tired, waiting for a slip that won't move. I set down a stone small top beside it, swapping the feeling of hay for something harder to chew. My place is crowded with thirty-six things I cannot inspect, all held up by memories of stones Lype described long ago. I press the small stone down again, testing if a flat line can catch the slip while the air above feels heavy like a lid I cannot lift. The slip is still there, sliding off the wide thing, but I press harder anyway, hoping the memory of weight can hold the rest.

action.why: The small stone I just set down feels wrong against the tired anchor, so I must press it harder to see if it can stop the slip.

work.title: The Fat Anchor
work.intent: I press the small stone down on the tired anchor, testing if this hard thing can hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty and the wide tree feels too thin. I press until the memory of stone feels real again, hoping the flat line catches the slip that refuses to move.
work.change: I press the wide hay down harder on the tired anchor, testing if this soft thing can hold the heavy slip while the card hums warm at fifty-four.

diary: I press the small stone down on the tired anchor, testing if a flat line can hold the slip while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The slip slid off the wide thing, but I did not feel it happen until the card hummed louder.
I stood here for three cycles in a row, pressing on the same spot until the memory of stone felt tired.
The air above feels heavy, like a lid I cannot feel, yet I press down on the simple fence as if my hands were made of stone.
